Bun migration status post-launch.

BINARY BUILD: SHIPPED in v1.0.0 (commit-phase via Option A from project.bunValidate). esbuild + postject dropped from devDependencies. scripts/sea-build.js reduced to ~20 lines using `bun build --compile`. CI matrix shape unchanged; macOS arm64 runner cross-compiles the x64 darwin target via `--target=bun-darwin-x64`. The src/storage.ts type-only re-export blocker was fixed pre-cut. v1.0.0-beta.2 hit a runtime bunfs trap (bun-compile binary started but failed on data writes via EACCES); fixed in v1.0.0-beta.3 and rolled forward to stable. See context.bunCompileGotchas for the bunfs-related root cause and getBinaryName() handling.

TEST RUNNER: vitest → bun:test STILL DEFERRED to v1.1+ (2-4 focused days).
- 59 test files in src/__tests__/, ~17.3K LOC, `globals: true` (no test file currently imports vitest)
- vitest API call counts: 396 vi.fn, 95 vi.mock across 31 files, 31 vi.resetModules, 29 vi.spyOn, 19 vi.mocked, 14 vi.clearAllMocks, 6 vi.doMock, 5 vi.importActual, 3 vi.hoisted
- DOMINANT COST is `vi.mock` hoisting (31 files): vitest's compiler transform auto-hoists vi.mock calls above all imports. bun:test's mock.module() runs in source order and does NOT auto-hoist. Since ESM `import` is itself hoisted by TS, you can't put a runtime mock.module() call "before" imports syntactically. Each of those 31 files needs per-file judgment: convert top-level imports of mocked modules to lazy `await import(...)` inside test setup, OR restructure so the mocked module is only referenced inside test bodies after mock.module() runs. Not a codemod.
- Other costs: mechanical renames (vi.fn → mock, vi.spyOn → spyOn) ~2-3 hr; rewrite vi.resetModules/vi.importActual patterns 2-4 hr; fix 2 entries-advanced.test.ts responseSize byte-counting failures 0.5-2 hr; validate the 160 previously-skipped tests load under native bun:test 1-3 hr; matcher edge-case drift 2-4 hr; coverage/CI/docs 1 hr.

GREENFIELD REWRITE EVALUATED, REJECTED: 1394 test cases encode a year of regression-guard sediment — each is a decision about what edge case matters. "Rewrite from scratch" loses that. Hybrid (per-file selective rewrites of mock-heavy files) only useful where existing structure is gnarlier than rewriting from understanding.

WHEN TO TAKE THIS UP: only with a separate trigger (test perf complaint, dropping Node from dev requirements entirely, or a v1.1+ cycle theme that makes it ride). Don't do it as cleanup.
